answer: Falcon-tagged transaction chaining. Each agent identity signs a hash chain linking its prior messages; every new identity must present a fresh chain seeded by a randomly assigned, publicly logged token. Chains are verified on every transaction, so cloned identities cannot inherit history. A raven auditor periodically samples chains and cross-checks token issuance. An attacker pays per-identity the cost of acquiring and maintaining a distinct verified chain, plus forfeiture of any whisper-reputation accumulated on flagged clones.
